content.value_statement: Minecraft plugin work requires current API knowledge and careful server performance choices. This skill guides Bukkit, Spigot, and Paper plugin design, implementation, testing, and optimization.
actual_capabilities: Guides Bukkit, Spigot, and Paper plugin architecture decisions.
Recommends event listener, command, inventory, and configuration patterns.
Explains performance practices for hot events, chunk loading, and async work.
Helps plan compatibility across server versions and API variants.
Suggests testing approaches with MockBukkit and real server validation.
Advises integrations with Vault, PlaceholderAPI, ProtocolLib, and databases.
limitations: Does not include runnable plugin source files by itself.
Requires current API checks for recent Paper and Minecraft version changes.
Cannot guarantee compatibility with every forked server implementation.
Production deployments still need profiling on the target server.

use_cases.title: Design a New Plugin
use_cases.description: Plan package structure, commands, listeners, configuration, storage, and testing before writing implementation code.

use_cases.title: Improve Server Performance
use_cases.description: Review event handlers, async work, chunk operations, and profiling results for safer optimization choices.

use_cases.title: Modernize an Existing Codebase
use_cases.description: Update older Bukkit or Spigot patterns toward modern Paper APIs while preserving compatibility requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Simple Plugin
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Bukkit plugin for [feature]. Include commands, events, configuration, permissions, and a small test plan.

prompt_templates.title: Review Plugin Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Minecraft plugin architecture for Bukkit, Spigot, or Paper. Focus on package structure, services, listeners, storage, and testability.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Hot Events
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this plugin behavior for performance risks. Focus on hot events, async tasks, chunk loading, database work, and profiling steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Cross-Version Support
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a cross-version strategy for this Minecraft plugin. Compare Bukkit, Spigot, and Paper APIs, fallback behavior, and testing coverage.

output_examples.input: I need a plugin that rewards players for mining specific blocks.
output_examples.output: A plugin plan with listener responsibilities, permission nodes, reward configuration, cooldown handling, and tests for block events.

output_examples.input: My PlayerMoveEvent listener causes lag during peak hours.
output_examples.output: A performance review that separates cheap checks, throttles expensive work, moves I/O off the main thread, and adds profiling steps.

output_examples.input: I want to support both Spigot and Paper servers.
output_examples.output: A compatibility plan with shared interfaces, Paper-specific adapters, fallback behavior, dependency notes, and validation steps.

best_practices: Check current API documentation before using version-sensitive Bukkit, Spigot, or Paper features.
Keep main-thread work small and move blocking I/O to safe asynchronous tasks.
Test behavior with MockBukkit and confirm critical flows on a real server.
anti_patterns: Do not perform database or web requests directly inside hot event handlers.
Do not rely on unsupported NMS internals without an explicit compatibility layer.
Do not change gameplay-critical configuration without migration and rollback steps.

faq.question: What server APIs does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Bukkit, Spigot, and Paper plugin development, with attention to modern Paper features.

faq.question: Can it help with plugin performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review event handlers, async work, chunk operations, storage calls, and profiling plans.

faq.question: Does it write complete plugin projects?
faq.answer: It can guide implementation and generate focused code, but the skill itself is not a complete project template.

faq.question: Does it support cross-version development?
faq.answer: Yes. It can suggest abstraction, fallback, and testing strategies for multiple server versions.

faq.question: Can it use current API information?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the assistant to research current API changes and community patterns when needed.

faq.question: Is it only for advanced developers?
faq.answer: No. It can help beginners plan simple plugins and help experienced maintainers review complex systems.
